mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of corporate existence and good standing for each proposed corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation (e.g., Companies House, Corporations Canada, State Administration for Market Regulation in China)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the issuing state is party to the Apostille Convention; otherwise full consular legalization through Global Affairs Canada and the relevant foreign ministry

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of passport or national photo identity document for each director, officer and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport/national identity authority of the individual's country of nationality
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization depending on the document's country of origin; recognized by Quebec corporate service providers and financial institutions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incumbency / register of directors and officers of the proposed corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or assistant secretary of the shareholder entity, or the official corporate registry in its jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized and affixed with Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization if executed in a non-Hague jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney appointing a Quebec attorney or registered agent to conduct name clearance and file incorporation documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Each proposed corporate shareholder and/or beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille if the power of attorney is signed outside Canada in an Apostille member state; alternative consular legalization for non-member states

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based customer due diligence for all directors, officers, UBOs and authorized signatories prior to incorporation, consistent with FINTRAC Guidance on Politically Exposed Persons and Heads of International Organizations. Screen against: (1) the United Nations Consolidated List; (2) Canada's Consolidated Autonomous Sanctions List under the Special Economic Measures Act; (3) the OFAC SDN List; (4) the UK HMT Consolidated List; and (5) EU financial sanctions lists. Enhanced due diligence, including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation, is required for any PEP or high-risk jurisdiction nexus. All screening results must be dated, documented, and retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire d'entreprises du Québec – Registre des entreprises (REQ) / Entreprises Québec; online portal: https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11), the corporate legal name must have a French form; a French legal element (e.g., 'Incorporé'/'Inc.', 'Société', 'Corporation' in its French usage) is mandatory. Names must be capable of being rendered in the Latin alphabet; ideographic, Cyrillic or non-Latin-script names require transliteration and a French legal name. A non-French brand name may be added as a secondary name or used with a trademark exemption, but the official registered name in Quebec must satisfy the French-language statutory rules.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: architect, engineer, notary, attorney, barrister, solicitor, physician
royal, government, municipal, crown, commission, agency
police, RCMP, Olympic, Red Cross, United Nations
words contrary to public order, morals or national security
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On rejection, the Registraire provides written reasons. The applicant may file a written request for reconsideration within 30 days of the refusal, attaching submissions and any revised distinctive element. If the registrar maintains the refusal, the applicant may apply to the Court of Québec for judicial review under Article 529 et seq. of the Code of Civil Procedure, CQLR c C-25.01, within 30 days of the reconsideration decision. A renewed name reservation application with a new distinctive element may be filed at any time.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for a low-risk silicone fidget manufacturer only if the virtual office provider maintains a physical commercial premises in Quebec, accepts service of process, and provides physical access to corporate records during business hours. Pure mail-forwarding or telephone-answer-only service addresses are not compliant. Virtual offices may increase banking KYC scrutiny and the likelihood of registrar verification.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: low, approximately 5% in the first year for a clean low-risk toy/fidget business; risk rises to approximately 15% if the registered office is a virtual service address, if complaints are lodged with the Registraire, or if UBO filings are inconsistent. Health Canada product-safety inspections under the Canada Consumer Product Safety Act are non-routine for this product class absent a safety or hazardous-materials complaint.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Quebec Business Corporations Act (QBCA), CQLR c S-31.1, ss. 37 (articles of incorporation), 49 (share subscription), 81 (registered office) and 152 (written resolutions); Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44 (alternative federal incorporation route)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), online through the Services Québec portal at www.registraire.gouv.qc.ca
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Statuts constitutifs) filed with the REQ; issuance of a Certificate of Incorporation and automatic enterprise registration (NEQ)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; shares may be issued for money, property or past services (not future services), with the subscriber's contribution paid before the shares are fully paid; no escrow account or banker's attestation is required for a non-public QBCA corporation
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED THAT: (1) The corporation subscribes for and issues 1,000,000 common shares listed in Schedule A at $0.01 per share, fully paid in money by the subscriber named therein; (2) The registered office is fixed at [address, Quebec], judicial district of [district], as declared in the Articles of Incorporation, where process may be served; (3) The following persons are appointed officers: [Name], President and Chief Executive Officer, and [Name], Secretary-Treasurer, with powers conferred by the by-laws; (4) Officers are authorized to execute all filings necessary to complete incorporation, open corporate bank accounts, and register with Registraire des entreprises du Québec, the Canada Revenue Agency, and Revenu Québec.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Reservation and NUANS Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), online name reservation module
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an optional NUANS search to verify name availability, then file the Demand of Name Reservation with the REQ specifying the legal element (Inc. or Corp.), distinct element (e.g., FidgetTech), and descriptive element (Silicone Sensory Products). Reservation fee is CAD 30 and the reservation is valid for 90 days. A numbered name (e.g., 12345678 Canada Inc.) may be adopted without reservation.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name and its constituent elements
NUANS search report or numbered name request
Statutory declaration on the choice of name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for confusion or a prohibited element, file a revised reservation with a stronger distinct element, adopt a numbered name, or contest the refusal within 30 days under the Regulation respecting business names.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), online incorporation filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the Articles of Incorporation (Statuts constitutifs) with the corporate name or number, registered office address in Quebec (no post-office box), authorized share capital (one or multiple classes with rights, privileges, conditions and restrictions), restrictions on business if any, and first directors (minimum one; no Canadian residency requirement under the QBCA). Pay the CAD 322 filing fee online, sign electronically and submit. The REQ issues the Certificate of Incorporation and creates the enterprise (NEQ) file.
required_dossiers: Name reservation certificate issued by the REQ
Completed and signed Articles of Incorporation
Consent to act of each first director
Registered office address in Quebec
Details of authorized share capital and director names
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the REQ issues a notice of deficiency, correct the articles online within 30 days using the regularization module; defects not cured may be remedied by filing Articles of Amendment (QBCA s. 155); no late penalty applies if corrected within the statutory period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Meeting and First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: First board of directors of the corporation (internal corporate records; no government filing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the directors' organizational meeting or adopt a written resolution in lieu of a meeting under QBCA s. 152 to: (i) adopt the by-laws, (ii) fix the registered office and judicial district, (iii) approve the pro-forma first board resolution covering share subscription, office adoption and officer appointments, (iv) allot and issue the common shares subscribed in Schedule A, (v) approve the minute book, corporate seal and banking resolutions.
required_dossiers: Pro-forma first board resolution
Directors' written consents
Draft by-laws of the corporation
Minute book, share register and share certificates
Banking resolution and authorized signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the subscription consideration is non-cash property, obtain a sworn valuation declaration; if the issue price is queried, revalue the property and adjust the share allotment to preserve the officers' liability protection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Enterprise Registration, Business Number and Tax Account Enrolment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ); Canada Revenue Agency (CRA); Revenu Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the automatic NEQ enterprise file created by the REQ and file the declaration of registration after incorporation. Apply to the CRA (RC-59) for the 9-digit Business Number with GST/HST, payroll and corporate income tax accounts, and register with Revenu Québec for QST (9.975%) and employer contributions. Update the enterprise description of activities to NAICS 339930 / ISIC 3240 in the registry. Open a corporate bank account supporting SWIFT/TT and platform payment rails.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and Articles of Incorporation
REQ registration statement / NEQ extract
CRA Business Number application (RC-59)
Revenu Québec QST and employer registration forms
Corporate bank account mandate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA queries the RC-59 because the activity description is vague, resubmit with NAICS 339930 and a precise production description; voluntary disclosure can remit late-registration penalties by backdating the account to the date of first sale or employer obligation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CNESST Employer Registration and Municipal Occupancy Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST); host borough or MRC municipal authority; local fire safety service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register as an employer with CNESST within 60 days of incorporation, before the first employee starts work. Obtain from the municipality the building occupancy certificate confirming light-industrial zoning compliance and the Quebec Construction Code; secure the fire safety permit under the Fire Safety Code (CQLR c Q-2, r. 8); provide the engineer's attestation of structural loading for compression molding presses where requested. Conduct a workplace risk assessment before commissioning.
required_dossiers: CNESST employer registration form
Lease or proof of ownership of the industrial premises
Occupancy certificate / building permit application
Fire inspection report and fire permit
Engineer's attestation of structural load (if presses exceed 10 tons)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the occupancy certificate is refused on zoning grounds, file a municipal zoning variance (dérogation mineure) or relocate to a conforming industrial zone; CNESST registration delays are cured by immediate filing and may result in retroactive premiums, which can be mitigated by written employer registration proof.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP), industrial projects authorization directorate; host municipality for sewer discharge
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Determine whether the silicone compression molding facility requires a certificate of authorization under Section 22 of the Environment Quality Act (EQA, CQLR c Q-2). Small fidget-toy molding operations are generally exempt from the full impact assessment but must keep total VOC emissions at or below 10 t/year, discharge wastewater only to a compliant municipal sewer, store silicone scrap as non-hazardous residual material with a permitted carrier, and file an attestation letter to MELCCFP before commissioning describing inputs, mass balance, emissions and waste streams. Use water-based mold-release agents to reduce VOC load.
required_dossiers: Mass balance of raw materials (silicone rubber, pigments, mold-release agents)
VOC emission calculation worksheet
Safety data sheets of all chemicals used
Residual materials management agreement with a permitted carrier
Municipal sewer discharge permit application, if connected
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MELCCFP reclassifies the project as requiring a Section 22 certificate of authorization, initiate the public-consultation application promptly (processing up to 90 days); alternatively reduce VOC usage to remain under the exemption threshold and request a formal exemption confirmation letter from MELCCFP.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie (Direction de l'industrialisation); Registraire des entreprises du Québec; CNESST; host municipality urbanisme service
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sector-specific statutory license applies to novelty fidget toy manufacture (ISIC 3240 / NAICS 339930); the required operational clearances are the municipal occupancy permit, CNESST employer registration and, where triggered, the MELCCFP certificate of authorization or attestation under Section 22 of the EQA; product safety compliance with the Canada Consumer Product Safety Act and Toy Regulations (SOR/2011-17) remains mandatory

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category: Exempt from the mandatory impact assessment procedure (not listed in the Règlement relatif à l'évaluation et l'examen des impacts sur l'environnement); registration or attestation under EQA Section 22 applies only where atmospheric VOC emissions exceed 10 t/year; otherwise a simple MELCCFP attestation letter suffices
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: VOC emissions ≤ 10 t/year; particulate emissions ≤ 100 mg/m³; wastewater discharged to municipal sewer must meet municipal by-law limits (pH 6.0–9.5, TSS ≤ 350 mg/L, BOD5 ≤ 350 mg/L) or zero-discharge if no sewer connection; silicone scrap classified as non-hazardous residual material disposed through a permitted carrier; prohibition of CFC/HCFC propellants in mold-release products

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification under the Quebec Fire Safety Code (CQLR c Q-2, r. 8), structural load inspection certified by an engineer for molding presses, building occupancy certificate from the host municipality, CNESST workplace health and safety registration, and employer first-aid compliance prior to commissioning

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Federal: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), portal canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html and My Business Account; Provincial (Quebec): Revenu Quebec, portal revenuquebec.ca and CLICK. Since 2013, Revenu Quebec administers both federal GST/HST and Quebec QST for Quebec businesses under a single-administration agreement; customs/export reporting is handled by the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) through the Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the Business Corporation federally under the Canada Business Corporations Act (Corporations Canada) or provincially under the Quebec Business Corporations Act (Registraire des entreprises du Quebec, REQ), obtaining the unique provincial NEQ identifier. Step 2: Obtain the federal 9-digit Business Number (BN) - automatic for federal incorporations; for Quebec incorporations, apply through CRA Business Registration Online or the REQ/Revenu Quebec one-stop service. Step 3: Register program accounts under the BN: RT (GST/HST), RM (customs import/export), RP (payroll), and RD (excise) as applicable. Step 4: Through Revenu Quebec one-stop online registration, open the QST (TVQ) account, the provincial payroll account, and the federal GST/HST RT account; Revenu Quebec issues the QST registration number and coordinates the federal RT account with CRA. Step 5: Enrol in CBSA's CERS and validate the RM customs account for goods exports. Step 6: Non-resident foreign entities may voluntarily register for GST/HST and QST by submitting the foreign incorporation certificate, board resolution, foreign tax identifier, and a Canadian address for service; registration is mandatory where the non-resident carries on business in Canada and taxable supplies exceed the CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold. Books, records, and the BN must be retained normally for six years from the end of the relevant reporting year.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A Business Corporation (Inc./Corp.) is a separate taxpayer subject to federal Part I corporate income tax and Quebec provincial corporate income tax; no pass-through eligibility exists under Canadian law. Resident corporations are taxed on worldwide income (with foreign tax credits for foreign business income); non-resident corporations are taxed only on Canadian-source income, generally through Part I tax and Part XIII withholding. Quebec maintains no general tax-exempt zone, and the ISIC 3240 novelty fidget toy compression-molding business qualifies for no statutory tax holiday.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada prohibits US-style check-the-box elections; entity classification follows statutory corporate law. Relevant statutory elections for this scope: (1) closely related corporation election under ETA s. 156 and its QST counterpart, deeming intercompany supplies at nil consideration to eliminate GST/QST friction; (2) functional-currency election under ITA s. 261 (e.g., USD for the exporter); (3) ITA s. 216 election for non-residents with net-basis Canadian rental income; (4) hybrid mismatch rules under ITA ss. 18.4-18.6, 91.6, and 247.11-247.13 (with Quebec counterparts) operate as mandatory BEPS Action 2 overrides - deduction disallowance or income inclusion - and are not elective.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax: federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) at 5% plus Quebec Sales Tax (QST/TVQ) at 9.975%, jointly administered by Revenu Quebec for Quebec businesses; the Harmonized Sales Tax (HST) does not apply in Quebec. Both taxes use an invoice-credit mechanism with input tax credits/refunds (ITCs/RTI) on taxable supplies of goods and services made in Canada, imports, and deemed supplies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 - the small-supplier threshold under ETA s. 148 and provincial equivalents. Registration is mandatory when worldwide taxable supplies of the person and associated persons exceed CAD 30,000 either in a single calendar quarter or over the four immediately preceding consecutive calendar quarters; registration is voluntary below the threshold and is available to non-residents.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, or digital stamping regime exists in Canada or Quebec. CRA requires electronic filing of GST/HST returns for monthly and quarterly filers (NETFILE/e-file); Revenu Quebec requires electronic transmission of the combined GST/QST return via CLICK. E-invoicing is being adopted voluntarily under the Pan-Canadian Trust Framework based on PEPPOL/BIS, with no government invoice clearance or API pre-validation. Taxpayers must retain commercial invoice data and export evidence in machine-readable form for six years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: A supply of silicone stress-relief fidget toys manufactured in Quebec is zero-rated at 0% GST and 0% QST where it is a sale of tangible personal property exported by the supplier or recipient under ETA s. 1 of Part V, Schedule VI (QST equivalent), i.e., the goods are delivered to an export carrier or transferred to the recipient for export from Canada and are exported as soon as reasonably possible (CRA administrative position generally expects export within 60 days from sale/delivery), with sufficient written evidence. Services: separately supplied services to a non-resident are zero-rated under ETA s. 7, Part V, Schedule VI only if the non-resident is not in Canada when the service is performed or the service is performed wholly outside Canada. Failure to substantiate converts the supply to taxable at 14.975% with risk of ITC reversal. No trade permit or special license conditions zero-rating for this novelty toy product.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs Invoice / Commercial Invoice in English or French identifying the supplier, BN, HS classification (ISIC 3240 goods, generally HS 3926/9503), unit values, and foreign consignee
CERS Export Declaration (Form B13A) filed electronically through the Canadian Export Reporting System for goods valued above CAD 2,000 or where a permit is required, with the CBSA confirmation number
Transport document: original Bill of Lading (ocean) or Air Waybill (air) with the carrier's certificate of export/loading
Proof of physical export and foreign receipt: foreign customs entry, destination clearance record, terminal receipt, forwarder's certificate, or courier delivery confirmation
Payment/foreign-currency evidence: SWIFT MT103 inward remittance credit or platform pay-out statement matching the invoice and evidencing receipt of proceeds from the non-resident buyer
For zero-rated offshore services (if any): executed contract with the non-resident's foreign address and written proof that the service was performed outside Canada
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Canada imposes no statutory FX repatriation deadline; however, ITA s. 247 transfer-pricing principles require arm's-length collection terms for intercompany receivables, and overdue balances can attract attribution adjustments. CRA and Revenu Quebec may deny zero-rating and reassess at 14.975% (GST 5% + QST 9.975%) with clawback of claimed ITCs/RTIs where export documentation is missing or inconsistent. The normal reassessment window is four years (ETA s. 298), extended without limitation in cases of misrepresentation, fraud, or wilful default. Civil penalties include a late-filing penalty of 5% of the net tax plus 5% per complete month up to 12 months (maximum 65%) and gross-negligence penalties for false statements equal to the greater of CAD 250 and 25% of the tax payable (ETA s. 285.1; Quebec Tax Administration Act ss. 59-60); interest compounds daily at the prescribed rate. Criminal exposure arises under ETA s. 327 and the Customs Act for tax evasion or false export statements, carrying corporate fines (up to CAD 25,000 per count on indictment), imprisonment of directors/officers, forfeiture, and exclusion from federal programs.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); foreign exchange policy and oversight are administered jointly with the Department of Finance Canada and the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI), with cross-border currency reporting enforced by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility under the Currency Act and the Bank of Canada Act. The Canadian dollar is a freely floating currency with no exchange controls, no central bank approval requirement for inward or outward remittances, and no restrictions on the repatriation of dividends, interest, royalties, or invested capital. Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is governed exclusively by Part XIII withholding tax under the Income Tax Act (generally 25% unless reduced by treaty, e.g., Canada-United States Income Tax Convention, and further reduced for provinces such as Quebec where abatement applies); applicable corporate rates of 5-15% apply depending on the shareholder's jurisdiction of residence. The practical hurdles are documentary rather than regulatory: source-of-funds evidence, CRS/FATCA self-certification, and Quebec's registraire des entreprises (REQ) good-standing attestation are routinely required by Canadian financial institutions to evidence the legitimacy of cross-border flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada does not impose statutory export-proceeds surrender timelines, mandatory conversion ratios, or repatriation windows. Exporters may lawfully retain foreign-currency proceeds in offshore or onshore foreign-currency accounts, invoice in USD or any freely convertible currency, and convert at commercial rates. The only compliance duties are indirect: accurate export declarations to the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) for customs and trade statistics, and FINTRAC reporting of every incoming or outgoing cross-border currency transfer of CAD 10,000 or more, together with record-keeping obligations under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA).

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / Local Quebec Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium (ancillary use only). The Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA), overseen by the Bank of Canada, now requires any payment service provider operating in Canada to be registered; however, offshore digital EMIs are not recognized as deposit-taking institutions under the Bank Act (Canada) and cannot lawfully open primary internal settlement accounts for a Quebec business corporation. Foreign EMIs (e.g., Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer) may be used as supplementary collection and disbursement corridors for marketplace payouts and small-ticket supplier payments, provided such providers hold a valid RPAA registration or operate through a regulated Canadian Schedule I bank partner. Primary treasury liquidity and statutory capital escrow must reside with a regulated Canadian bank or provincial credit union.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Not generally mandatory. Canadian Schedule I banks accept remote and video-identified onboarding for low-risk private corporations; nonetheless, at least one authorized signing officer or director must complete identity verification through a notarized attestation or an in-person meeting where the bank's risk-based approach requires it. A Quebec-resident officer, director, or registered agent materially accelerates onboarding and reduces enhanced-due-diligence triggers. Mandatory documentation comprises the federal Certificate of Incorporation and articles (or provincial Quebec 'constitución' file), REQ Quebec enterprise registration attestation, beneficial-ownership declaration, CRS and FATCA self-certification forms, current corporate resolutions authorizing account opening, and a physical-nexus proof such as a lease or registered office agreement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO) where a non-resident parent or a trust holds silent or indirect control
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete UBO declaration listing full legal name, date of birth, residential address, nationality, and precise percentage of shares and voting rights for every natural person owning 25% or more; certified extract of the corporation's share register; signed declaration from the Quebec registered agent attesting to the accuracy of the register; certified passport and proof-of-address for each identified UBO; and, where relevant, a trust deed or ownership-flow chart evidencing the legitimate commercial rationale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient physical and operational nexus in Quebec, raising shell-company indicia
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: REQ attestation in good standing; commercial lease, serviced-office agreement, or sublease evidencing premises in Quebec; Quebec TP-1 provincial tax registration and GST/QST registration certificates; payroll or contractor records if personnel are engaged; corporate bank statement history with active operating transactions; product-liability insurance certificate; and the website, purchase orders, and supplier agreements evidencing a live business.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Aggregated platform-payment inflows from marketplace settlements that do not clearly map to traditional invoiced receivables
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Platform settlement statements covering at least the last 12 months; merchant agreements with the marketplace or payment processor; customer transaction logs sufficient to reconcile aggregated payouts; commercial invoices and tax-inclusive receipts; reconciliation workpaper linking each platform payout to underlying e-commerce sales; and a signed AML/CFT compliance statement from the treasury officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity cross-border supplier disbursements to low-cost manufacturing jurisdictions inconsistent with the stated low-risk profile
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed supplier framework agreements and purchase orders; commercial invoices quoted under Incoterms 2020; ocean or air waybills (bills of lading); Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) customs entry records with HS classification 3924/4014 and country-of-origin documentation; freight forwarder delivery proofs; certificates of compliance for food-grade silicone (e.g., FDA 21 CFR 177.2600 or LFGB); and bank reference letters from the supplier's financial institution confirming commercial legitimacy.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: No exchange-control or central-bank pre-approval is required. Inbound shareholder capital is remitted via SWIFT MT103 to the Canadian operational account with Field 70 reference line clearly stating 'Paid-in capital / shareholder equity contribution' and the corporate name. The remitting shareholder must remit from their own bank account, and the Canadian bank may request source-of-funds evidence for credits of CAD 10,000 or more. Every cross-border transfer of CAD 10,000 or more is subject to FINTRAC large-cross-border-transaction reporting. The company must retain the signed subscription agreement, board resolution approving the share issuance, the updated share register or securities ledger, and the CRS/FATCA self-certification of the non-resident shareholder to prove the equity (not debt) character of the funds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Routine supplier payments for component materials and third-party logistics are executed by SWIFT MT103 through the relationship bank's correspondent network, with the beneficiary bank identifier (BIC) and correct ISO 20022 structured remittance references where supported. Larger and purchase-order-backed disbursements against firm production commitments are cleared via Commercial Letter of Credit (L/C), issued by the Canadian bank in favor of overseas suppliers and confirmed, where necessary, by a receiving bank in the supplier's jurisdiction. CAD/USD settlement occurs onshore at the relationship bank's desk rate or upon a transactional request-for-quote; all outbound disbursements are reconciled against the approved treasury budget, supplier invoices, and CBSA customs declarations to preserve audit integrity.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forwards (CAD/USD) executed with a Canadian Schedule I relationship bank, fully permitted for commercial hedgers without derivative-license requirements
FX Vanilla Options and zero-cost collar structures (CAD/USD) for bounded downside protection, permitted as treasury hedging rather than speculative dealing
Cross-Currency Swaps (CAD/USD) for matching long-term foreign-currency asset and liability streams, subject to board-approved counterparty limits

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) are technically accessible through Canadian banks but are generally unnecessary and discouraged for CAD, which is fully convertible, except in exceptional illiquid-market circumstances

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than the last day of the month following the month of the corporation's registration anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD 22; repeated failure permits cancellation of enterprise registration and loss of legal personality

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary of the date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative dissolution after one year of default; revival possible only by application with arrears fees and notarial reinstatement

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Corporation Income Tax Return (Form T2)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the fiscal year-end; balance due on the last day of the second month after year-end (third month for qualified CCPCs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month up to 12 months, compounded daily interest, and possible criminal prosecution for wilful non-filing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the fiscal year-end; balance due on the last day of the second month after year-end (third month for qualified CCPCs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 5% late-filing penalty on unpaid tax plus 1% for each full month of delay, non-deductible interest, and administrative collection enforcement including Scopus seizure

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue-based threshold; audit is mandatory for reporting (public distribution) corporations and for private corporations unless all shareholders unanimously approve a waiver of the appointment of an auditor under Section 229 of the Quebec Business Corporations Act or Section 163(2) of the Canada Business Corporations Act.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for public reporting enterprises; Canadian GAAP for private enterprises (ASPE, Part II of CPA Canada Handbook) accepted for non-reporting Canadian business corporations; any financial statement delivered to directors must comply with GAAP

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: At each annual director review, the corporation must confirm and update its register of individuals with significant control (ISCs) within 15 days of any change; no standalone UBO report is filed with the regulator for private CBCA/QBCA corporations, but the register must be available for lawful inspection by CRA, Revenu Québec, and enforcement authorities.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 160–450 per year for registered office and statutory records address in Quebec
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 2,800–7,500 per engagement for a small private manufacturing corporation, depending on transaction volume and bookkeeping quality

stage_6.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report gross worldwide revenue from active business operations before expenses; exclude non-resident-source income allocable to foreign permanent establishments claimed via Form T2203.
